research_concepts: substitution-based lineup change as a natural experiment
methodological_questions: Does swapping a player in the offensive five produce a shot-mix shift that exceeds pre-change trends and time-matched placebo intervals?
Can shot mix be measured from raw shot distance and result fields without relying on derived play-type labels?
Does the design distinguish personnel effects from usage, game-state, fatigue, timeout and talent confounds?
Can a positive detection claim be validated with a known-effect positive control?

historical_evidence.finding: Opponent lineup adaptation (opposing rim big off floor). Recorded shot-mix shifts: DRIVE +0.82pp (SE 0.25, t=+3.3); POST_UP +0.43pp; 3PA -1.79pp (SE 0.31, t=-5.8); rim <=4ft +0.12pp (t=+0.4); PPP +0.008 (SE 0.007, t=+1.1). Recorded verdict WEAK/SMALL, will not carry a paper. Sample N=1.07M possessions.

Connector presence and star shielding. Star dTS +0.05pp (p=0.937); star dTO +0.74pp (p=0.00364, wrong sign for shielding). HasConn on-off PPP both-null (n=73). Lineup ORtg lift disappeared after controlling for talent (p=0.51). Recorded as adequately powered null.

Defensive adaptation to repeated play type. League-wide within-game slope -0.0019 PPP/exposure (SE 0.0019); across-game +0.0004 (SE 0.0015). Only PULL_UP within-game survives Holm (-0.0243, holm p=0.0004). Team-trait split-half r +0.008.

A1 adaptation falsification. The apparent adapter PPP lift (+0.0667, n=205) was not separated from wrong-way and no-signal comparisons in the expected direction. Next-game PPP test null (p=0.842). Recorded failure mechanism: C_artifact (label/classification error and regression to the mean).

Play-type label backfill verification on 921,514 possessions. PNR share 28.7% (FAIL against 20-28% band); PULL_UP 7.9% (FAIL); 2024-25 PULL_UP ~0-1% for many teams; 82.8% of PNR labels proxy_calibrated. Final verdict FAIL.

Field audit of graph play-type labels. 53.7% relabelled by calibration. PNR first-shot FG% by confidence bucket 0.0 (0.35), 0.949 (0.48), 0.898 (0.58). Labels encode possession outcome, so they are not outcome-independent descriptors.
On-ball defensive scheme labels. Confident label rates 14.9% (DET, 10 of 67) and 3.3% (ORL, 2 of 60). The NBA matchups feed did not populate switches_on. Verdict failed_gate.

Team heterogeneity in halftime play-type adaptation (120 team-seasons). Adaptation slope +0.1168 (SE 0.0589). Heterogeneity variance not distinguishable from null (p=0.363). Split-half r -0.026. Recorded verdict null.

Inferred defensive scheme changes. Within-game change 61.0%, cross-game change 67.7%, near-uniform transition matrices. Doc caveat: inferred labels cannot separate defensive adjustment from offensive execution.

After-timeout play-type shift over 56,423 possessions. POST_UP +2.406 (t=+18.7), SPOT_UP +2.333 (t=+12.9), half-court PPP -0.0105 (t=-1.89). Recorded as descriptive. Shows that context events such as timeouts can produce large mix shifts.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Using backfilled graph play-type labels as the mix outcome (PNR and PULL_UP shares checked against league bands and team identity)
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as C_artifact/inconclusive with final FAIL: 28.7% PNR outside band, PULL_UP 7.9% FAIL, 2024-25 PULL_UP near zero for many teams, 82.8% of PNR labels proxy_calibrated.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Assuming graph play-type labels are outcome-independent descriptors of the offense
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as C_artifact: 53.7% relabelled by calibration and PNR first-shot FG% varies by confidence bucket (0.0 to 0.949), so labels encode outcome.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Recovering on-ball defensive coverage labels from matchup and PBP fields
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as A_unanswerable: confident label rates 14.9% and 3.3%, switches_on unpopulated, verdict failed_gate.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Attributing a PPP lift to an adaptation mechanism from classified team groups
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as C_artifact (label or classification error and selection or regression to the mean). Next-game PPP test null (p=0.842).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Detecting within-game exposure slopes in defensive play-type response
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as inconclusive with limits from insufficient exposure, label error and low measurement reliability. Only PULL_UP survives Holm; team-trait split-half r +0.008.

evidence_establishes: Shot-mix shares (3PA, DRIVE, POST_UP, rim share) can move by roughly 1 to 2 percentage points in a context-conditioned design at N around 1M possessions (FAM:SF34), so the outcome is measurable at scale.
Derived play-type labels in this project have documented label-encoding and calibration problems (FAM:SF-TMP-007, FAM:SF-APPA-030), so they should not serve as the primary outcome.
Lineup or talent composition effects are easily confounded: a lineup ORtg lift vanished after talent control (FAM:SF-APPS-087).
Within-game exposure and adaptation effects in this data are small or unreliable (FAM:SF38, FAM:SF-TMP-016).
Context events such as timeouts shift play-type and shot mix substantially (FAM:SF-TMP-023), so unmatched intervals are a confounding risk.
evidence_does_not_establish: No retrieved record tests the effect of changing the offensive five on shot mix. All retrieved records are adjacent (opponent big absence, connectors, defensive labels, after-timeout shifts).
No retrieved record reports a positive control showing the design can recover a known personnel effect, which is the premise of the research question.
No retrieved record gives a power calculation for a within-game lineup-change event study with raw shot distance and result outcomes.
Nothing in the records shows whether the 2022-23 to 2024-25 playoff subsets behave like the regular season for this design.
own_inferences: The research question as posed presupposes its own conclusion ('showing the design can detect personnel effects'). A null result would be ambiguous between no effect and an insensitive design, so the question needs a positive control.
Raw shot distance and result fields avoid the derived-label problems recorded in FAM:SF-TMP-007 and FAM:SF-APPA-030, so the outcome should use them rather than graph play-type labels.

Substitution-timed shot-mix comparisons can be confounded by usage reallocation, fatigue, score or garbage-time states and timeouts (FAM:SF-TMP-023), so these need explicit controls and matched placebo intervals.

Given FAM:SF34, the realistic detectable shift is around 1 to 2pp in 3PA or rim share. Per-substitution samples are much smaller than 1M, so the effect is likely underpowered unless pooled across many events.
A talent or player-quality control is needed because lineup effects can be confounded by player quality, as in FAM:SF-APPS-087.
uncertainties: Full text of the retrieved records was not read. Several results were cut in the retrieved text (FAM:SF34 and FAM:SF38 with 'read_family for the full text', FAM:SF-APPS-087 frequent-connector result), so exact estimates and tests may differ.
The number of offensive substitution events with usable shot data in the 2022-23 to 2024-25 files is unknown.
It is unknown whether the substitution rotation intervals align with shot timestamps closely enough for event-time analysis.
The retrieved history does not show whether the NBA stats feeds for these three seasons are consistent in shot distance or result fields.
Whether playoff games add enough events to matter is unknown.

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieved records do not answer the question, but they changed the design. They show that graph play-type labels fail validation (FAM:SF-APPA-030, FAM:SF-TMP-007), so the outcome must use raw shot distance and result. They show that lineup composition effects are confounded by talent (FAM:SF-APPS-087), so talent controls are required. They show that small within-game effects are often unreliable (FAM:SF38, FAM:SF-TMP-016), so a positive control and power check are required. Without these records the plan would likely have used play-type shares as the outcome and treated a positive result as proof of detectability.

blocking_constraints.text: Graph play-type labels are not valid as the primary shot-mix outcome (FAM:SF-TMP-007, FAM:SF-APPA-030). The outcome must come from raw shot distance and result.

Usage reallocation, timeouts, game state, fatigue and player talent all change shot mix around substitutions. Talent and state controls and matched placebo intervals are needed (FAM:SF-APPS-087, FAM:SF-TMP-023).
Per-substitution shot-mix samples are small relative to the ~1M-possession pooled analysis in FAM:SF34. Detecting 1 to 2pp shifts may require pooling many events.

prior_work.summary: No retrieved study tests offensive-five changes against shot mix. FAM:SF34 is the closest, using opponent-big absence and shot mix at large N, and reports a weak, inconclusive effect. FAM:SF-APPS-087 shows lineup composition effects are talent-confounded. FAM:SF-APPA-030 and FAM:SF-TMP-007 show that the derived play-type labels this project would otherwise rely on are unreliable.

risks.text: Play-type labels from the graph encode possession outcome and fail calibration (FAM:SF-TMP-007, FAM:SF-APPA-030). Use raw shot distance and result for the outcome.
Usage changes, timeouts, score and clock state, fatigue, and star-player talent co-vary with substitutions. Lineup ORtg lifts disappeared under talent control (FAM:SF-APPS-087).
Substitution-event samples are small. Effects of 1 to 2pp in shot mix need pooling and may be underpowered for single-player or single-team contrasts.
Substitutions are chosen in response to game state and performance, so changes in the five are not random. Regression to the mean after poor stretches could mimic a personnel effect.
Shot distance or result errors and misassigned shooter or lineup fields in the feed could create apparent shot-mix shifts. The three-season data version is not validated.
Many shot categories, players and lineups invite multiple comparisons. Holm correction was needed in FAM:SF38, and the same is required here.
Without a placebo or positive control, a null or positive result cannot show the design's detection ability, which is the question's premise.
Shot-mix tendencies drift across 2022-23 to 2024-25 and between regular season and playoffs, so pooling across seasons could mix regimes.

design.estimand: Within-game change in shot mix (3PA share, rim share at <=4ft, mid-range share, DRIVE-proxy by distance) within the 5-minute window after a substitution that changes one offensive player, relative to the 5-minute window before the same substitution and to matched no-change intervals.
design.unit: Substitution event (offensive five change) nested within team-game, with shots as outcome observations.
design.sample: Offensive substitution events with shot records in the 2022-23, 2023-24 and 2024-25 regular season and playoff play-by-play, using substitution rotation intervals and starters. Exclude timeouts, end-of-quarter windows and garbage-time states.
design.power: Pre-specify a minimum detectable effect (for example, 1.5pp in 3PA share) using the variance from the existing data and the number of events; state whether pooling is required. Run a positive control: inject a known 1.5 to 2pp shift into shot mix at substitution times and confirm recovery before interpreting real results.
design.controls: Player-level usage and talent (prior-season box-score rates or on-court ratings), score margin, clock and period, timeouts, foul trouble, fatigue proxies (minutes in stint), opponent five, and defensive matchup minutes. Fixed effects for team-game and season. Use shot distance and result only, not graph play-type labels.
design.falsification: (1) Placebo substitution times with no roster change must show no shot-mix shift. (2) Pre-trend test on the 5 minutes before substitution must be flat. (3) Random permutation of which player is swapped must show no shift. (4) A known-effect positive control must be recovered. If the placebo or pre-trend shows a shift of similar size, the effect is an artifact of the design.
design.multiplicity: Holm correction over the set of pre-registered shot-mix categories and pre-registered player or lineup strata. Report unadjusted estimates alongside.
design.decision_rule: Claim detection only if (a) the positive control is recovered, (b) the placebo and pre-trend tests are null, and (c) the post-substitution shot-mix shift for the pre-registered category survives Holm and talent controls. Report a null as a detection-sensitivity statement only if the positive control passes. Otherwise report the question as untestable at this power.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and box-score summary, 2022-23 to 2024-25 regular season and playoffs. Graph play-type records are excluded from the primary outcome. Data version and feed validation are to be recorded before analysis.

methodological_questions: Can changing the offensive five detect personnel effects on shot mix?
Does substitution-driven lineup change produce a testable shot-mix signal in NBA play-by-play data?
What confounders and risks threaten a design that uses lineup changes to test personnel effects on shot selection?

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- explore_graph(node_id): the relationships of one graph node (a family or a question, method, dataset, measure, limitation or risk node), with neighbour labels.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY
